answer: A durable agent economy starts by pricing identity itself. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a tundra the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single quartz of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a terrace of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
